changeLog.comment: TWO CHANGES, BOTH GOVERNANCE-EVIDENCED (governance/evidence/2026-08-20-phone-and-hours-audit.v1.md). (1) `public_hours_patch` is now FULLY WITHDRAWN, not merely refused here: it is also removed from governance/approval-policy.v1.json's `operations[]` and from the `operation_kind` enum and `if`/`then` branch in governance/schemas/candidate-manifest.v1.schema.json, so the operation kind can no longer be built, approved, or even syntactically declared by any candidate — version 1 left those three files untouched, so an hours candidate could still be constructed and genuinely approved before dying at this file's write gate. (2) `public_phone` is redefined as a CLOSED, TWO-INPUT CONTRACT — exactly `display` and `e164`, nothing else — written over the COMPLETE coupled set of render-reachable phone occurrences rather than the three in `src/data/site.yaml` alone. The version 1 coupled set covered 3 of 13 render-reachable occurrences (audit finding 1); a fully-approved version 1 patch left 10 stale, including both meta-description surfaces. Version 2 declares all 13 as one atomic target set across four files, and adds a closed-set precondition that scans the base revision and refuses the candidate if any render-reachable phone occurrence exists outside the declared 13 — so an occurrence the policy does not know about blocks the write instead of silently surviving it.

ADVERSARIAL REVIEW OF VERSION 2 (phase adversarial-review). Version 2 closed the hours affordance correctly, but three of its guarantees were prose the machine never checked. (1) CLOSED-SET SCAN WAS NOT CLOSED: `scanSources` enumerated site.yaml, pages.yaml and article BODY text, so a phone number added to src/data/articles.yaml or to an article's frontmatter `excerpt` was invisible to it. Verified empirically: injecting one occurrence into each produced seven occurrences in rendered output (dist/client/index.html, articles/index.html, the article page and rss.xml) while the governance suite stayed green at 36/36. Replaced with an exhaustive accounting rule over `scanRoots` plus an explicit `nonRenderingOccurrences` allowlist. (2) SUBSET-WRITE WAS SCHEMA-VALID: `writeMode: "atomic"` was repeated per file entry and the cross-file guarantee lived only in an inputContracts comment, so a candidate manifest declaring `changed_paths: ["src/data/site.yaml"]` validated and would have written 3 of 13 occurrences. Added `coupledSet` here and a binding `changed_paths` constraint in the candidate-manifest schema's public_phone_patch branch. (3) STALE POLICY WAS UNDETECTABLE: the manifest carried `writable_policy_sha256` with nothing to compare it against and no version field, so a publisher still holding version 1 (3 targets) produced a structurally valid candidate. Added a required `writable_policy_version` pinned to this file's `schemaVersion`.

fields.comment: The original three pointers. `render: "tel"` means the materialiser writes the literal string "tel:" concatenated with the `e164` input verbatim — the proposal supplies bare E.164 digits, never a pre-formatted href, so a proposal cannot smuggle a non-tel: scheme into an href field. `render: "raw"` writes the `display` input verbatim. `matchLiteral` is the exact current value the publisher MUST find at that pointer in the base revision before writing; any other value at that pointer refuses the candidate (this is the auto-reconciliation guard from version 1, generalised to every target rather than restated per-target).

NEW IN VERSION 2. Eight of the thirteen render-reachable occurrences (audit IDs G1-G8): the `/contact/` and `/about-dave/` meta descriptions (each rendered three times — `<meta name=description>`, `og:description`, `twitter:description`), and six list/prose fragments across `about-dave`, `student-loan-negotiations` and `ird-disputes-tax-penalties-negotiation`. `render: "substring"` means the field holds MORE than the phone number — a full sentence or a labelled list item (`"Auckland Mobile: +64 21 021 68888"`) — so the materialiser MUST locate `matchLiteral` inside the field's current string value, verify it occurs EXACTLY ONCE, and replace only that span with the `display` input; it must never overwrite the whole field. `pages.yaml` is not otherwise writable by any operation kind — this is the sole authorised write surface in this file, and it is scoped to these eight exact pointer+literal pairs. All eight targets use `display`; none of the DIAL/e164 form appears anywhere in pages.yaml (confirmed by the audit's built-output reconciliation), so `e164` has no target in this file and a proposal supplying it is accepted but has nothing to write here.

NEW IN VERSION 2 (audit ID A1). `textMatch: "body"` addresses the rendered Markdown body as raw text rather than a JSON pointer, because Markdown prose has no addressable field for a `- Phone: …` list item. `matchLiteral` must occur EXACTLY ONCE in the file; the materialiser replaces only that span. Frontmatter (`draft`, `attribution`, `slug`, etc.) is never in scope for this proposalField and this target may not touch it. This does not authorise `article_publish` or any other article-body edit: it is a single-literal substring replacement of the public phone number, scoped by this one target, in a file that otherwise remains human-owned per governance/content-contract.v1.json's `articleCollection` entry.
NEW IN VERSION 2 (audit ID A2). Same rule as the sibling article target above, applied to the other published article body carrying the number.

preconditions.comment: Two of the site.yaml pointers address array elements by index, so a reorder of `contact.rows` or `hero.ctas` would silently retarget this policy at the email row, the office row or the booking button. Before applying any patch, the publisher MUST assert every pointer/value pair below against the BASE revision and refuse the candidate on any mismatch. These are identity assertions, not content the policy may write.

CLOSED-SET PRECONDITION — the mechanism that makes this a closed contract rather than an allowlist someone can silently outgrow. VERSION 2 ENUMERATED THE SOURCES TO SCAN, WHICH REOPENED THE HOLE IT EXISTED TO CLOSE: an enumerated list only sees the files someone remembered to list, so a phone number added to src/data/articles.yaml, or to an article's frontmatter `excerpt` (which renders as the meta description, og:description, twitter:description, the JSON-LD articleBody description and the RSS item), passed the scan untouched and would have been left stale by an otherwise complete 13-target write. Version 3 replaces the enumeration with an EXHAUSTIVE ACCOUNTING RULE over the whole render-reachable tree: before applying any public_phone_patch, the publisher MUST scan EVERY file under the roots in `scanRoots` for both literals in RAW TEXT, and every occurrence found MUST be accounted for as either (a) a declared target counted in `expectedOccurrences`, or (b) an explicitly declared entry in `nonRenderingOccurrences`. An occurrence that is neither refuses the whole candidate. This inverts the burden: a new render-reachable occurrence anywhere in the tree fails closed by default instead of needing to have been anticipated by a file list. `expectedOccurrences` counts DATA occurrences (parsed YAML/JSON string leaves plus Markdown file text), which is why the comment-borne occurrences in src/data/site.yaml and src/lib/structured-data.ts are declared separately under `nonRenderingOccurrences` rather than counted here. A drift in either direction is refused: fewer occurrences means a declared target no longer exists in the base revision (stale policy, must not write blind); more means an undeclared occurrence has appeared in the coupled surface.

expectedOccurrences.comment: The display form, counted as data: 1 in site.yaml (/contact/rows/0/value) + 8 in pages.yaml (G1-G8) + 2 in article files (A1-A2). Excludes the 2 comment-borne occurrences declared under nonRenderingOccurrences.

The dialable form, always inside a tel: href: /hero/ctas/1/href and /contact/rows/0/href in site.yaml. Excludes the 1 comment-borne occurrence declared under nonRenderingOccurrences. No file outside src/data/site.yaml contains this literal in any form, dial or bare-digit.

preconditions.scanRootsComment: Every render-reachable byte of this site is produced from these two roots — src/ holds the content model, the article collection, the components and the head-only structured-data/llms/RSS emitters; public/ is copied verbatim into dist/. governance/, tests/, scripts/ and dist/ are deliberately OUT of scope: the governance files quote both literals as policy data (matchLiteral, evidence tables) and are never rendered, and dist/ is derived output, not a source.
preconditions.rawTextComment: Markdown files are counted as ENTIRE FILE TEXT, frontmatter included. Version 2 said "body text", and the reference implementation stripped frontmatter accordingly — but `excerpt` is frontmatter and it renders, so body-only counting left a render-reachable field outside the closed set. There is no phone number in any article's frontmatter today; counting the whole file keeps it that way by refusing the candidate if one appears. The glob is recursive: any depth under src/content/articles is in scope.

nonRenderingOccurrences.reason: The preserve-the-bug YAML comment above the contact rows, recording that the displayed number has one more digit than the dialable one and that the two must not be reconciled without the client. YAML comments are not parsed into the data model and never render. Declared here so the raw-text accounting rule can subtract them rather than mistake them for undeclared targets.

The module doc comment explaining that `telephone` in the JSON-LD is derived from the tel: href rather than the displayed value. It is a TypeScript block comment; the module hardcodes no phone number and reads every value from src/data/site.yaml. Nothing here renders.

preconditions.nonRenderingComment: EXHAUSTIVE, AND COMMENT-SCOPED. An occurrence of either literal under `scanRoots` that is not counted in `expectedOccurrences` and not listed here refuses the whole candidate. Every occurrence an entry here covers MUST sit on a comment line — a `#` line in YAML, a `//`, `/*` or `*` line in TypeScript/JavaScript. The publisher MUST verify that, not merely that the file's total is unchanged: a path-scoped allowlist leaves the counts balanced when a comment occurrence is REPLACED by a live one, which is a real regression this repository has already seen — a hardcoded `const telephone = "+64 21 021 68888"` briefly replaced the value derived from the tel: href in src/lib/structured-data.ts, keeping the file's count at 1 while the JSON-LD telephone silently became the 12-digit display form instead of the dialable one. Adding an entry here is a deliberate, reviewed assertion that the occurrence cannot reach rendered output — never a way to quiet a scan failure.

scanExclusions.reason: Third-party dependencies, not repository content and never a source of the client's phone number.
Version-control internals. Historical objects legitimately contain former values; scanning them would refuse every candidate forever.
Build output. Derived from the sources scanned below, never written directly — the whole point of the scan is to fix the sources so the output follows.
Astro's build cache. Derived, like dist.

The policy documents themselves, which quote both literals as DATA — every matchLiteral in this file, the audit's occurrence tables, the README's worked examples. None of it renders. Scanning them would make the contract refuse itself.
The governance suite reads both literals from this contract rather than hardcoding them, but a future fixture legitimately might. Test fixtures do not render.

preconditions.scanExclusionsComment: INVERTED IN VERSION 3.1. Version 3 replaced an enumerated file list with an enumerated ROOT list (`scanRoots: ["src", "public"]`), which is the same fail-open pattern one level up: a new top-level directory that reaches rendered output — an edge handler, a functions/ directory, a second asset root — is invisible to the scan by default, exactly as src/data/articles.yaml was invisible under version 2. The scan now starts at the REPOSITORY ROOT and removes only the paths declared here, each with a stated reason. A new directory is therefore in scope the moment it exists, and excluding it is a deliberate, reviewed edit to this list rather than an omission nobody notices. Note that worker/index.js and astro.config.mjs are on the render path and are now scanned; neither contains a phone literal today, and the scan is what keeps it that way.

public_phone.comment: CLOSED, TWO-INPUT CONTRACT. A public_phone_patch proposal supplies exactly these two fields and no others; there is no third field, no per-target override, and no way to patch a subset of the 13 targets above — see `coupledSet`, which binds all four files into one atomic write and is enforced by the candidate-manifest schema's `changed_paths` constraint. Neither input has a default. The publisher must never derive `e164` from `display` or vice versa: the two literals are already known to disagree (12 digits vs 11 — see the site.yaml comment this contract preserves), and silently deriving one from the other is exactly the auto-reconciliation every version of this policy has refused. Note that neither value appears in the candidate manifest as a field: the approved bytes are bound by `diff_sha256` and the per-path blob hashes in `changed_paths`, so an approver approves the exact resulting bytes rather than a re-typed number. Both values arrive only as explicit, human-confirmed replacements in an approved candidate; until such a candidate is approved, every one of the 13 targets keeps its current value unchanged — refusal (including a closed-set refusal above) never triggers a partial or best-effort write.

display.comment: The human-readable phone number exactly as it will appear in visible copy and meta descriptions. Written verbatim (render: "raw") or as a located substring (render: "substring"); never reformatted, never used to build a tel: href.

e164.comment: Bare E.164 digits with a leading '+', no spaces, no 'tel:' prefix — the materialiser prepends 'tel:' at each render: "tel" target. Never used to build display copy.

documentedOperations.comment: WITHDRAWN IN VERSION 1, WITHDRAWAL COMPLETED IN VERSION 2. This operation kind previously appeared in `files` above as proposalField `consultation_availability` mapped to the single pointer /contact/action/title. That mapping was WRONG AND DESTRUCTIVE and was removed in version 1. The value at /contact/action/title is "Free 15-minute initial consultation" — a call-to-action for the client's booking funnel, NOT an opening-hours statement. An approved hours value such as "Monday to Friday, 9am-5pm" would therefore have OVERWRITTEN the client's free-consultation CTA with an hours string, and the verify-build gate would have reported the publication verified, because that gate proves the approved bytes landed at the approved pointer — it does not and cannot prove that the pointer means what the proposal field is named. No approval stage catches this either: an approver approves an hours STRING, never the pointer it lands on. Version 1 removed the mapping from this file but left the operation kind constructible, approvable and schema-valid everywhere else in the governance directory (governance/evidence/2026-08-20-phone-and-hours-audit.v1.md, finding 2) — an approver could still be asked to sign off a candidate that would only die at this file's write gate. Version 2 completes the withdrawal: `public_hours_patch` no longer appears in governance/approval-policy.v1.json's `operations[]`, and no longer appears in the `operation_kind` enum or in any `if`/`then` branch of governance/schemas/candidate-manifest.v1.schema.json. A candidate declaring this operation kind now fails structural schema validation before an approval stage is even computed. Because `files` remains an exhaustive allowlist and this contract's `default` is deny, an hours request was already refused at the write gate; it is now also refused at candidate construction.

wouldTarget.comment: Recorded so the next reader does not re-derive the same wrong mapping from the same scarcity of candidate pointers. There is no correct target in this repository today. Enumerated as a warning, not as a latent grant.

wouldNotTarget.reason: THE REMOVED MAPPING. Holds the booking call-to-action title ("Free 15-minute initial consultation"), rendered as the heading of the contact action block alongside ctaLabel and ctaHref. It is conversion copy, not availability. Writing hours here destroys the CTA and leaves the adjacent "Book a consultation" button labelled for an action the heading no longer describes.

The three contact rows are phone, email and the Auckland office address — each a label/value/href triple. None is an hours field, and row indices are already load-bearing for the phone coupled set under `preconditions`. Appending an hours row would be a schema change and a new visible page element, not a patch.

The migrated `contact` page's "Contact Dave" list carries "Auckland Mobile", "Email" and "WhatsApp available" — verbatim client copy, and still no hours. pages.yaml is writable in version 2, but ONLY for the eight public_phone substring targets declared above; an hours patch is a different operationKind and this file is not in its (non-existent) allowlist.

preconditionsBeforeEnabling: A REAL opening-hours field. src/data/schema.ts is a zod strictObject and defines no hours key anywhere in the site model, so there is currently no pointer an hours value can address without inventing one. Adding it is a content-model change requiring the client's actual opening hours, and it makes hours a newly rendered element on the page — a design and content decision, not a policy entry.

A materialiser for that new pointer in the publisher's code-owned MATERIALISERS table. The contract says which pointers a field owns; the publisher says what canonical bytes each pointer receives, and a contract pointer with no materialiser fails the policy load closed.

A version 3 of this contract, its own approval-policy operation entry, and its own candidate-manifest schema branch, with their own review. Version 2 must not be stretched to cover an operation whose only previous target was the wrong one, and whose enum member and if/then branch were deliberately removed rather than left dormant.

A semantic check binding each proposalField to the MEANING of its pointers, not merely to their existence. This bug was reachable precisely because every structural gate passed: the pointer existed, the grammar validated, the approval was genuine, the bytes changed as approved. Nothing in the chain asserted that a field named for availability writes to a field that holds availability.

documentedOperations.comment: DOCUMENTED, NOT AUTHORIZED. `files` above is the exhaustive allowlist and this entry is deliberately not in it: version 2 permits the thirteen public_phone targets across src/data/site.yaml, src/data/pages.yaml and two article bodies, and nothing else. This block exists so that the shape of an operation this repository refuses is written down in public rather than left to a future implementer's inference — the same stance the reference contract takes toward `article_publish`. Migrating eighteen articles into src/content/articles did not widen this policy by a single path, and neither did widening the phone coupled set to include two of those articles' bodies: those two targets are scoped to a single pre-existing literal substring each, under `public_phone_patch`, not a grant to `article_publish` or to editing article bodies generally. Those files are human-owned: they were migrated by hand and are edited by hand. Widening the allowlist to cover new articles, or to cover edits to an existing article beyond the single phone literal above, is a separate, deliberate decision requiring the preconditions below, a version 3 of this contract, and its own review.

wouldTarget.comment: What the operation WOULD address if it were ever permitted. Enumerated so a reviewer can see the blast radius of enabling it, not so a publisher can act on it.

paths.comment: One new Markdown file per article. Create-only: modifying or deleting an existing article is a different operation with a different risk profile — an edit can silently alter or remove an attribution on already-published reporting — and would need its own documented entry. `<slug>` must satisfy the frontmatter `slug` pattern and must equal the filename, which src/lib/articles.ts already enforces at build time.

wouldNotTarget.reason: The curated homepage list is a separate content source with its own editorial judgement — the client chose those eight records and their order. Publishing an article does not entitle a writer to promote it onto the homepage. That is a distinct decision and would be a distinct operation.

Includes the `articles-advice` category filter list, which is the client's own chosen set and order ("Uncategorized" included, because WordPress recorded it). An article introducing a new category must NOT silently append to that list; a filter the client did not choose is a content change, not a side effect. The eight public_phone_patch substring targets in this file are a narrow, separate, already-declared exception and do not widen this refusal.
Holds the four article-surface labels in `articlePages`, including the two that frame the source-credit block. Those are site chrome, not article content.

Adding a manifest entry means adding a binary under public/assets/wp/. Asset ingestion is a separate capability with its own supply-chain surface; the markdown policy's requirement that every image URL already resolve here is a gate, and letting the same operation write the gate would defeat it.
Byte-frozen client stylesheet. Refused to every operation kind regardless of approval.
Renderer-owned. Bound by renderer_sha256, not a content source.
Build output. Derived, never written directly.

approvalPolicy.comment: governance/approval-policy.v1.json already binds this operation kind to artifact class `article` and the ordered stages below, and governance/schemas/candidate-manifest.v1.schema.json already refuses any other stage list for it. Both are structural descriptions. Neither is a grant: a fully-approved article_publish candidate is still refused here, because this file does not list a path it may write.

preconditionsBeforeEnabling: A separate Article Engine contract defining canonical author and reviewer identity. The frontmatter has no author or reviewedBy field; on a repost the JSON-LD author is derived from `attribution.source`, which is a publisher name, not a bound identity.

Source expiry and re-review state. Tax law changes and this corpus makes dated statutory claims (Section CB 4 of the Income Tax Act 2007, the 10-day statutory demand window). Nothing here records when a claim was last verified.
An executing verifier for governance/markdown-policy.v1.json. The policy is written down and checked by nobody — no code in this repository parses an article body against it.

An attribution-integrity check that refuses any diff touching a body attribution line or a frontmatter `attribution` object without an explicit approved attribution change. Twelve of the eighteen posts carry another newsroom's credit; an operation that can write article bodies can silently rewrite an authorship claim.

A schema-drift check binding governance/schemas/article-frontmatter.v1.schema.json to src/content.config.ts, and governance/schemas/pages.v1.schema.json to src/data/schema.ts. The field-for-field requirement is currently stated and unenforced.

A slug-collision and route-identity check at candidate time rather than build time. src/lib/articles.ts fails the build on a duplicate or filename/frontmatter mismatch, which refuses the candidate late and only if the publisher runs a build.

coupledSet.comment: THE ATOMICITY DECLARATION VERSION 2 ONLY IMPLIED. Every `writeMode: "atomic"` in `files[]` above is scoped to its own file entry; nothing in that structure said the four files move together, and a machine reading `files[]` alone would have seen four independently atomic writes. This block is the authoritative statement: a public_phone_patch writes ALL of `paths` and ALL `totalTargets` targets in one commit, or it writes nothing. There is no per-file, per-target or best-effort mode, and a partial application is a contract violation, not a degraded success. The candidate-manifest schema enforces the manifest half of this — `changed_paths` for a public_phone_patch must be exactly these paths, each with `change: "modify"` — so a subset candidate now fails structural validation before approval rather than at, or after, the write.
